leads.title: French Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810
leads.documents: Decriminalisation of same-sex sexual activity in private in France and colonies that adopted the Code, including French Guiana as overseas department.
leads.detail: Cited as Penal Code of 1791 making no mention of same-sex relations in private, retained in Penal Code of 1810; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Penal Code Article 330 alinea 2 - Mirguet amendment (1960) and repeal (1980); March 2024 compensation bill
leads.documents: Former discriminatory indecent exposure law doubling penalty for homosexual activity, its repeal, and National Assembly unanimous bill for compensation to gay men arrested under Article 330 prior to 1980.
leads.detail: Cited as ordonnance 1960 inserting Article 330 2nd alinea on proposal of Paul Mirguet, repealed 1980; March 2024 National Assembly bill, Senate yet to vote; no URL visible

leads.title: French Penal Code Article 225-1 and Labour Code Chapter 2 - Discrimination protections (1985, 2012, 2016)
leads.documents: National ban on sexual orientation discrimination (1985), addition of sexual identity (July 2012) replaced by gender identity (18 November 2016); Labour Code ban on exclusion/sanction/dismissal on grounds including sexual orientation and gender identity.
leads.detail: Cited as law of 1985, law of July 2012, law of 18 November 2016 amending article 225-1; Code du travail quote included; no URL visible

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 amending Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881 - Hate crime/speech law
leads.documents: Criminalisation of homophobic/sexist/racist comments, injury/defamation/insult/incitement; increased penalties when assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation; creation of Haute autorité de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'égalité (HALDE).
leads.detail: Cited as National Assembly amendment 31 Dec 2004, Title 3 and articles 20 and 21 amending 1881 Press Law; max penalty €45,000 and/or 12 months; Christian Vanneste conviction Jan 2006 cancelled by Court of Cassation; no URL visible

leads.title: PACS Law 1999 and Same-Sex Marriage Law 2013 - Constitutional Council Decision 17 May 2013, Journal Officiel
leads.documents: Legal recognition of same-sex couples via pacte civil de solidarité (1999) and full marriage equality (2013), stated as legal in all overseas departments and territories including French Guiana.
leads.detail: Cited as Government of Lionel Jospin 1999; National Assembly 329-229 on 12 Feb 2013, Senate approval 12 April, Assembly 23 April, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 May 2013, signed 18 May, published Journal Officiel next day, first ceremony 29 May Montpellier; no URL visible

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - B. vs France (1992)
leads.documents: Ruling that changed French ban on legal gender change, requiring France to allow legal gender change even after medical/surgical transition.
leads.detail: Cited as 1992 case B. vs France at European Court of Human Rights ending decades-long legislative ban; no URL visible

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on Modernisation of Justice (gender marker change effective 1 Jan 2017) - Constitutional Council 17 Nov 2016
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without surgery/sterilisation or psychiatrist certificates, via court order; first name change via registry office; 2017 aggravation for transphobic crimes.
leads.detail: Cited as Senate approval 6 Nov 2015, Assembly 24 May 2016 and 12 July 2016 modified version, Senate 28 Sept, Assembly 12 Oct, Constitutional Council constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov 2016, published Journal Officiel next day, effect 1 Jan 2017; no URL visible

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Report 2022 on gender affirming healthcare in France; Académie Nationale de Médecine position; Senate 2024 youth care report
leads.documents: Institutional/human-rights assessment documenting lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable access by location in France; recommendation for informed consent/self-determination model; subsequent medical-political controversy.
leads.detail: Cited as ILGA-Europe 2022 report; Académie Nationale de Médecine characterizing rise as epidemic-like; centre-right Senate commission of Little Mermaid Observatory March 2024 report, Senate passage May 2024 bill to ban medical transition under 18, opposed by Macron government; French Society of Pediatric Endocrinology late 2024 guidelines (Tanner stage 2 + puberty blockers); no URL visible

leads.title: DILCRAH - French Interministerial Delegation for Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism and Anti-LGBT Hatred (2022 controversy)
leads.documents: France's rights machinery for anti-LGBT hatred; documents institutional credibility issue when scientific committee president revealed as member of Little Mermaid Observatory which called gender-affirming care mutilation.
leads.detail: Cited as DILCRAH scientific committee controversy 2022, one member resigned, president stepped away from Observatory; no URL visible

leads.title: 16 May 2020 report on homophobic/transphobic attacks and 2014 overseas acceptance study + overseas deputies vote record
leads.documents: Enforcement/incident data: 36% rise in 2019, ~1,870 victims identified by police vs ~1,380 in 2018; overseas context: same-sex marriage legal in all overseas departments but lower acceptance, 20% overseas vs 77% metropolitan see homosexuality as like any other (2014 study); French Guiana deputies: 1 voted for same-sex marriage, 1 abstained of 27 overseas deputies.
leads.detail: Cited as report released 16 May 2020 before IDAHOTB; President Macron Oct 2018 denunciation after homophobic attacks; 2014 study figures; parliamentary vote breakdown listing French Guiana; no URL visible
